title: Brief committee meeting with consent agenda only
subtitle: A delegation raised Soper Park encampment evictions; the committee also received a respiratory pathogen report on consent.
overview: The Community and Health Services committee had a short meeting with no presentations and no items on the regular agenda. The only business was the consent agenda, which the committee received for information and approved {{vote:m1}}. It included the Waterloo Region respiratory pathogen report. No items were pulled for discussion.

A delegate arrived after the agenda had been dealt with and spoke about the encampment evictions at Soper Park in Cambridge in late September. The delegate said the approach taken did not respect the rights of people living in encampments and urged that residents be meaningfully engaged and offered acceptable alternative places to live. The delegate also questioned whether the earlier closure of the encampment at 150 Main was voluntary. No committee members asked questions, and no motion followed.
The meeting adjourned at 9:13 a.m. {{vote:m2}}. The next committee meeting is November 7, 2023.

decisions.detail: The committee received the consent agenda items, including the Waterloo Region respiratory pathogen report, for information and approved them {{vote:m1}}.

debate: A delegate said access to adequate housing is a major social determinant of health, and that municipalities, not only higher levels of government, share responsibility for upholding housing rights.

The delegate argued that people in homeless encampments should be treated as rights holders and be given information and a real say in decisions affecting them, rather than being criminalized or penalized.

The delegate said removing residents without meaningfully engaging them and identifying acceptable alternative places to live amounts to a forced eviction. The delegate said this did not happen at Soper Park, though the work of frontline and outreach workers was commended.

The delegate also said people who left the 150 Main encampment and moved to Soper Park did not describe their departure as voluntary, contrary to the Region's characterization. No committee members asked questions.
